
% --- Fix Horizontal Rules (---) ---
% Save the original \rule command so we can still use it later
\let\oldrule\rule

% Redefine \rule to check if it's the specific one generated by Pandoc for '---'
\renewcommand{\rule}[2]{%
  % Check: Is the requested width exactly 50% of the line width?
  % (Pandoc converts markdown '---' to \rule{0.5\linewidth} by default)
  \ifdim#1=0.5\linewidth
    \hrule % If yes, replace it with a full-width horizontal rule
  \else
    \oldrule{#1}{#2} % If no, draw the rule exactly as requested originally
  \fi
}

% --- Force Equation Numbering ---
% Redefine standard display math \[ ... \] to use the numbered 'equation' environment
% This ensures $$...$$ in Markdown gets numbered in the PDF
\renewcommand{\[}{\begin{equation}}
\renewcommand{\]}{\end{equation}}

\usepackage[most]{tcolorbox}

% --- Left-align all captions ---
% singlelinecheck=false stops LaTeX from centring captions that happen to fit
% on one line; justification=raggedright left-aligns the rest.
\usepackage[justification=raggedright,singlelinecheck=false]{caption}

% --- Left-align all section headings ---
% The KOMA classes that Quarto books use set headings with \raggedsection;
% make it explicitly ragged-right, so that a wrapped heading is never
% justified or centred.
\makeatletter
\@ifundefined{raggedsection}{}{\renewcommand*{\raggedsection}{\raggedright}}
\makeatother


% --- Color Definitions ---

\definecolor{thm-frame}{HTML}{CFE2FF}

% Definition
\definecolor{def-bg}{HTML}{F0FFF4}
\definecolor{def-frame}{HTML}{BADBCC}

% Example
\definecolor{ex-bg}{HTML}{FFFBF0}
\definecolor{ex-frame}{HTML}{FFEEBB}

% Proof
\definecolor{proof-bg}{HTML}{E2E3E5}
\definecolor{proof-frame}{HTML}{E2E3E5}

% Solution

% Algorithm

\definecolor{alg-frame}{HTML}{CE93D8} % Darker Purple frame

% --- Box Environments ---

% Theorem
\tcolorboxenvironment{theorem}{
  colback=thm-bg,
  colframe=thm-frame,
  boxrule=0pt,
  sharp corners,
  left=5pt, right=5pt,
  top=5pt, bottom=5pt,
  breakable
}

% --- Chapter macros used in several display equations ---
% \[ ... \] is an equation group above, so a \newcommand inside one display
% would vanish at its end. Define such macros here; the chapter keeps a
% \renewcommand inside its first display for MathJax (HTML).
\newcommand{\bx}[1]{\boxed{\mathtt{#1}}\!}

% --- Characters missing from Times New Roman or Latin Modern Math ---
% Superscript/subscript digits typed as Unicode in tables and text, check
% marks, and \setminus (U+29F5 is absent from latinmodern-math).
\usepackage{newunicodechar}
\usepackage{pifont}
\newunicodechar{⁰}{\textsuperscript{0}}
\newunicodechar{¹}{\textsuperscript{1}}
\newunicodechar{²}{\textsuperscript{2}}
\newunicodechar{³}{\textsuperscript{3}}
\newunicodechar{⁴}{\textsuperscript{4}}
\newunicodechar{⁵}{\textsuperscript{5}}
\newunicodechar{⁶}{\textsuperscript{6}}
\newunicodechar{⁷}{\textsuperscript{7}}
\newunicodechar{⁸}{\textsuperscript{8}}
\newunicodechar{⁹}{\textsuperscript{9}}
\newunicodechar{⁻}{\textsuperscript{\textminus}}
\newunicodechar{₁}{\textsubscript{1}}
\newunicodechar{₂}{\textsubscript{2}}
\newunicodechar{✓}{\ding{51}}
\newunicodechar{✗}{\ding{55}}
\AtBeginDocument{\renewcommand{\setminus}{\mathbin{\backslash}}}

% --- Code and printed output ---
% Wrap long source lines instead of running past the margin, and set code a
% size smaller and printed R output two sizes smaller.
% (\AtBeginDocument: Pandoc defines Highlighting after the header includes.)
\usepackage{fvextra}
\AtBeginDocument{%
  \RecustomVerbatimEnvironment{Highlighting}{Verbatim}{commandchars=\\\{\},breaklines,breakanywhere,fontsize=\small}%
  \RecustomVerbatimEnvironment{verbatim}{Verbatim}{breaklines,breakanywhere,fontsize=\scriptsize}%
}

% --- Fit gt tables to the text width ---
% gt sets its tables as \begin{tabular*}{width}{@{\extracolsep{\fill}}spec}, with
% fixed column widths that can add up to more than the line; gt-latex.lua
% rewrites them as \begin{gtfit}{width}{spec} (and maps gt's fixed 12pt/20pt
% fonts to the document's sizes). A table that fits is set at gt's width as
% before; a wider one is set at its natural width, and scaled down to the line
% width if needed.
\usepackage{environ}
\usepackage{adjustbox}
\newsavebox{\gtfitbox}
\NewEnviron{gtfit}[2]{%
  \sbox{\gtfitbox}{\begin{tabular}{#2}\BODY\end{tabular}}%
  \ifdim\wd\gtfitbox>#1\relax
    \adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\usebox{\gtfitbox}}%
  \else
    \begin{tabular*}{#1}{@{\extracolsep{\fill}}#2}\BODY\end{tabular*}%
  \fi
  \par}% end the line, so that gt's footnotes start below the table

% --- Place-value digit boxes (Computer Arithmetic chapter) ---
% The chapter writes its digit displays as math arrays with these macros;
% MathJax gets its own definitions in the chapter.
% \pvm mantissa, \pvs sign, \pve exponent, \pvz alignment zero (not stored),
% \pvx digit rounded off, \pvo no room, \pvn plain box, \pvh column heading.
\definecolor{pvm}{HTML}{E3EEFB}
\definecolor{pvs}{HTML}{FBE4EC}
\definecolor{pve}{HTML}{E7F6E0}
\definecolor{pvx}{HTML}{FDE0E0}
\definecolor{pvred}{HTML}{B22222}
\newsavebox{\pvsave}
% \pvbx{frame}{background}{text colour}{content}; at least 0.75em wide
\newcommand{\pvbx}[4]{%
  \sbox{\pvsave}{$\textcolor{#3}{\mathtt{#4}}$}%
  \ifdim\wd\pvsave<0.75em\sbox{\pvsave}{\makebox[0.75em]{\usebox{\pvsave}}}\fi
  {\setlength{\fboxsep}{2pt}\setlength{\fboxrule}{0.8pt}%
   \fcolorbox{#1}{#2}{\vrule width 0pt height 0.8em depth 0.25em\usebox{\pvsave}}}}
\newcommand{\pvm}[1]{\pvbx{gray!70!black}{pvm}{black}{#1}}
\newcommand{\pvs}[1]{\pvbx{gray!70!black}{pvs}{black}{#1}}
\newcommand{\pve}[1]{\pvbx{gray!70!black}{pve}{black}{#1}}
\newcommand{\pvn}[1]{\pvbx{gray!70!black}{white}{black}{#1}}
\newcommand{\pvz}[1]{\pvbx{gray!35}{white}{gray!55}{#1}}
\newcommand{\pvx}[1]{\pvbx{gray!70!black}{pvx}{pvred}{#1}}
\newcommand{\pvo}[1]{\pvbx{gray!70!black}{pvx}{pvred}{\mathbf{#1}}}
\newcommand{\pvh}[1]{{\scriptstyle\textcolor{gray}{#1}}}
